images.title: The full leap year rule
images.purpose: Recap the complete leap year rule as a short flow chart students can use to sort the years in any long span.
images.composition: Three decision diamonds in one horizontal row across the middle, each with a 'No' arrow dropping to a result box below, and a final 'Yes' arrow ending in a result box at the right; plenty of white space.
exact_structure: 3 decision diamonds outlined teal #0072B2, left to right: 'Divisible by 4?', 'Divisible by 100?', 'Divisible by 400?'
Between diamond 1 and diamond 2: a right arrow labelled 'Yes'; between diamond 2 and diamond 3: a right arrow labelled 'Yes'
From diamond 3 a right arrow labelled 'Yes' to a green #009E73 box '366 days'
Below diamond 1: a down arrow labelled 'No' to an amber #E69F00 box '365 days'
Below diamond 2: a down arrow labelled 'No' to a green #009E73 box '366 days'
Below diamond 3: a down arrow labelled 'No' to an amber #E69F00 box '365 days'
In total: 3 diamonds, 4 result boxes (2 green 366, 2 amber 365), 3 Yes arrows, 3 No arrows
rejection: the No arrow from 'Divisible by 100?' going to 365 days instead of 366 days
the Yes arrow from 'Divisible by 400?' going to 365 days
a count of diamonds other than 3 or of result boxes other than 4
any worked totals of days for a span of years
images.takeaway: A year has 366 days if it is divisible by 4 but not by 100, or if it is divisible by 400; otherwise it has 365 days.
images.description: A flow chart with three diamonds, divisible by 4, by 100 and by 400, leading to 366 day or 365 day result boxes.
images.context: Shown beside the practice on testing the leap year rules over long spans.
images.teaching_notes: Trace one year, such as 1900 or 2000, through the chart before counting the years of each kind.

image_decisions.why: A compact flow chart of the full rule is the tool students need for sorting years in the practice.
